meta.subtitle: Water and energy pumping-systems maker; Q2'26 net sales rose 6% to $622.9M and management raised full-year 2026 guidance.

analystSentiment.commentary: We rate Franklin Electric BUY with a target range of $105.00 to $125.00, against a current price of $95.99 as of 2026-09-23. That range matches the full width of the Street's target range and sits near the $118.50 consensus. Q2'26 net sales rose 6% to $622.9M, and operating income rose to $93.6M at a 15.0% operating margin. Growth came from all three operating lines and from about $15.0M of incremental sales from the Benson Pump and Wood Brothers Industries acquisitions closed in April and May 2026. Management raised full-year 2026 guidance to net sales of $2.21B to $2.29B and adjusted diluted EPS of $4.50 to $4.70. The balance sheet is net cash, and cash generation is steady. The counter-case is valuation and cyclicality: the shares trade at 27.7x TTM earnings and 12.3x TTM EV/EBITDA, the business is cyclical, and tariffs plus Argentine and Turkish currency exposure weigh on reported results. A $4.5M legal settlement in Energy Systems and a step-up in debt over the period temper the quarter.

executiveSummary.companyOverview: Franklin Electric Co., Inc. designs, manufactures, and distributes water and fuel pumping systems, serving residential, agricultural, municipal, industrial, and fueling applications in the United States and international markets. The company operates through three segments: Water Systems, Energy Systems, and Distribution. Water Systems supplies motors, pumps, water treatment systems, and electronic controls for groundwater, water transfer, and wastewater uses. Energy Systems makes pumps, piping, monitoring devices, and controls for fueling stations and other energy applications, including power-reliability and data-center infrastructure. The Distribution segment provides presale support and specifications to installing contractors and sells through wholesale, retail, and specialty distributors. The company was founded in 1944 and is headquartered in Fort Wayne, Indiana. FY25 revenue was $2.1B, up 5.4%, with FY25 diluted EPS of $3.22 and net income of $147.1M. The vendor's fundamentals feed reports FY25 as a single consolidated line; the 10-Q itself breaks results into the three operating lines used below, and we follow the filing.

thesis.label: BUY
thesis.body: Franklin Electric is a cash-generative water and energy infrastructure supplier trading at a premium multiple on a conservative balance sheet. Q2'26 net sales rose 6% to $622.9M and operating income rose to $93.6M, with growth in all three operating lines. Management raised full-year 2026 guidance for both revenue and adjusted EPS after the print. The bull case rests on water-treatment and dewatering demand, price realization, and bolt-on acquisitions; the bear case rests on the 27.7x TTM P/E, cyclical end-market demand, and tariff and currency headwinds. At $95.99, the shares sit below the $118.50 consensus target, which frames the reward against a real cyclical downside.

catalysts: Management raised full-year 2026 revenue and adjusted-EPS guidance after the Q2 print; delivery against the higher bar is the near-term catalyst to watch.
Benson Pump and Wood Brothers Industries added about $15.0M of incremental Q2'26 sales, and further bolt-on deals could extend the Distribution and Water Systems footprint.
Demand in higher-growth applications is building, with U.S. and Canada water treatment products up 14% and groundwater pumping equipment up 12% in Q2'26.
Tariff refunds lifted the Q2'26 gross margin to 37.0%, and a clearer trade-policy outcome could ease the input-cost overhang.
risks: Valuation leaves little room for error at the current premium multiple.
Demand is cyclical, tied to housing starts and to energy and mining end markets.
A $4.5M Energy Systems legal settlement weighed on that segment's Q2'26 margin.
Currency exposure to the Argentine Peso and Turkish Lira reduced Q2'26 results.

income.note: Source: Bigdata.com company tearsheet (FMP); fiscal years ended December 31.

financials.incomeCommentary: Q2'26 net sales were $622.9M, up 6% from $587.4M a year earlier, and six-month net sales were $1,123.3M, up 8%. Consolidated gross profit was $230.6M in Q2'26, a 9% increase, and the gross margin expanded to 37.0% from 36.1% a year earlier, helped by tariff refunds. For the six-month period, gross margin was essentially flat against the prior-year 36.0%, pressured by an unfavorable product and geographic mix. SG&A was $132.1M in Q2'26, or 21.2% of sales, up from 21.0%. Operating income increased to $93.6M in Q2'26, in line with the sales gain, and rose {+ 7% +} to $141.7M for the half. A $4.5M legal settlement in Energy Systems and $0.4M of restructuring sat in Q2'26 operating costs. GAAP diluted EPS was $1.46 in Q2'26, up $0.15, and adjusted diluted EPS was $1.55, {+ up 18% +}. Interest expense rose to $3.5M in Q2'26 from $2.8M on higher average debt, and the effective tax rate was 25.7% versus 24.9%. Across FY21 to FY25, revenue grew from $1.7B to $2.1B and the operating margin ran between 11.4% and 12.7%; FY25 diluted EPS was $3.22, down from $3.86 in FY24.

balance.note: Source: Bigdata.com company tearsheet (FMP); fiscal years ended December 31.

financials.balanceCommentary: The balance sheet stayed conservatively financed through the June 2026 quarter. FY25 net debt was -$67.8M, net debt to EBITDA was 0.0x, and TTM interest coverage was 23.5x, with a TTM current ratio of 2.41. Total assets, receivables, inventories, and equity all rose over the six months, reflecting an acquisition- and seasonally-driven working-capital build, while cash held roughly steady. Borrowing increased over the period, which lifted interest expense as noted, though leverage remained low against equity and cash flow. FY25 total debt was $31.8M. The net-cash position and the high coverage ratio leave room to fund acquisitions, buybacks, and the dividend without strain.

cashflow.note: Source: Bigdata.com company tearsheet (FMP); fiscal years ended December 31.

financials.cashflowCommentary: Franklin Electric converts earnings to cash consistently. FY25 free cash flow was $193.5M, a 9.1% FCF margin, and the TTM free cash flow yield was 5.1%. Across FY21 to FY25, free cash flow ranged from $0.1B to $0.3B, and FY25 capital expenditure was -$45.3M. The company reinvested through the Benson Pump and Wood Brothers Industries acquisitions during 2026 and continued to return cash to shareholders. Operating cash flow rose year over year in the six-month period, funding capital additions and the acquisitions.

multiples.note: Peer multiples pending a peer data source.

valuation.multiplesCommentary: At $95.99, the shares trade at 27.7x TTM earnings, 1.9x TTM sales, and 12.3x TTM EV/EBITDA. The forward multiples are lower, at 20.6x on next-twelve-month earnings and about 18.6x on FY27E earnings. Consensus estimates call for FY26E revenue of $2.3B and EPS of $4.65, and FY27E revenue of $2.4B and EPS of $5.16. The Street consensus target is $118.50, the median is $122.00, and the range runs $105.00 to $125.00, on a 2 Buy / 3 Hold / 0 Sell split. No peer multiples are in the pack, so the multiples stand on the company's own history and forward estimates. The premium earnings multiple reflects a quality water-infrastructure franchise, but it also assumes the raised 2026 guidance and FY27 growth are delivered.

scenarios.name: Bull
scenarios.driver: Raised 2026 guidance is met at the high end, and water-treatment, dewatering, and acquisition momentum carries EPS toward the FY27E $5.16; the multiple holds near the top of the Street's $105.00 to $125.00 target range.

scenarios.name: Base
scenarios.driver: Full-year 2026 net sales land within the $2.21B to $2.29B guide and adjusted EPS within $4.50 to $4.70; the shares re-rate toward the $118.50 consensus as mid-single-digit growth continues.

scenarios.name: Bear
scenarios.driver: Housing starts and energy and mining demand soften, tariffs and Argentine and Turkish currency losses pressure margins, and the premium 27.7x TTM multiple compresses on slower growth.

valuation.scenarioCommentary: The three scenarios put most of the probability on the base case, where Franklin Electric delivers the raised 2026 guidance and grows mid-single digits. The bull case assumes the top end of the guide and continued strength in water treatment and dewatering, taking the multiple to the upper end of the Street range. The bear case, at $80.00, is a real downside: it sits more than 15% below the current price and reflects the cyclicality the 10-K names, compounded by tariff and currency headwinds. The probability-weighted fair value falls within our target range and above the current price, which supports the BUY rating while acknowledging a genuine cyclical downside.

segments.name: Consolidated
segments.body: Franklin Electric reports one consolidated business built from three operating lines: Water Systems, Energy Systems, and Distribution. In Q2'26, Water Systems net sales were $358.5M, up 5%, with operating income of $65.2M at an 18.2% margin. Energy Systems net sales were $80.2M, up 3%, at a 34.8% operating margin, after a $4.5M legal settlement cut that margin 270 basis points from 37.5%. Distribution net sales were $221.1M, up 11%, at an 8.9% operating margin, improving 80 basis points. Consolidated Q2'26 net sales were $622.9M with operating income of $93.6M at a 15.0% margin. Intersegment profit on Water-to-Distribution transfers is deferred until the end-customer sale, which links the operating lines together.

moatFactors.name: Brand and technical position
moatFactors.body: The company describes itself as a global leader in systems and components for the movement of water and energy and a recognized technical leader in its products. Price realization contributed to growth in every segment in Q2'26, evidence of pricing power. The premium 27.7x TTM P/E reflects the market's view of franchise quality.

moatFactors.name: Distribution ownership
moatFactors.body: Owning the route to market gives Franklin Electric direct customer relationships and specification influence at the point of installation, which supports pricing and share. The Distribution operating line grew at a double-digit pace in Q2'26 and adds scale through bolt-on deals such as Benson Pump. That model extends the channel into new regions and product niches.

moatFactors.name: Margin and balance-sheet strength
moatFactors.body: TTM operating margin was 12.6% and TTM gross margin 35.5%, and consolidated operating margin was in the mid-teens in Q2'26. High interest coverage and near-zero net leverage give room to invest through cycles. Margins remain exposed to raw-material and tariff cost swings.

businessMoat.durability: Franklin Electric's durability rests on essential water and fueling infrastructure, recurring replacement demand, and a distribution channel that is hard to replicate quickly. The net-cash balance sheet noted above supports steady investment and bolt-on deals. The moat is not wide, because demand is cyclical and the company does not generally hedge raw-material costs. Tariffs and highly inflationary accounting in Argentina and Turkey add external volatility the company cannot fully control. On balance the franchise is durable but cyclical, consistent with a NARROW moat rating.

points: Q2'26 net sales grew 6% to $622.9M and six-month sales grew 8% to $1,123.3M.
The raised full-year 2026 outlook guides net sales to $2.21B to $2.29B and adjusted diluted EPS to $4.50 to $4.70.
Consensus estimates project FY26E revenue of $2.3B and EPS of $4.65, rising to FY27E revenue of $2.4B and EPS of $5.16.
Acquisitions contributed about $15.0M of incremental net sales in Q2'26, and management is investing in higher-growth water and energy applications.
Energy Systems sales outside the U.S. and Canada grew 12% in Q2'26 on European and African demand.

management.leadership: Joseph A. Ruzynski is Chief Executive Officer and is quoted in the Q2'26 release citing organic volume-growth initiatives and demand in dewatering for mining, pressure boosting, and water treatment. Jennifer A. Wolfenbarger is VP and Chief Financial Officer, having joined the company as CFO on July 7, 2025, after an interim CFO period and the March 2025 resignation of the prior CFO. The management team also includes segment presidents for Global Water, Headwater Companies, and Franklin Energy Systems, and a Chief Administrative Officer who serves as General Counsel and Corporate Secretary. The recent CFO transition is a watch item, though the appointment is now settled.
management.capitalAllocation: Capital allocation balances reinvestment, acquisitions, and shareholder returns against a net-cash balance sheet. During 2026 the company acquired Benson Pump and Wood Brothers Industries, funded from cash flow and borrowing. In FY25 it repurchased $165.6M of stock while keeping capital spending modest. The net-cash position leaves flexibility for further bolt-on deals. The dividend yields 1.18%, and management maintains stock-ownership requirements that align executives with shareholders.
management.governance: Governance rests on the DEF 14A proxy in the pack. The Board has determined that every current director except CEO Joseph A. Ruzynski is independent under NASDAQ standards. Jennifer L. Sherman has served as an independent, non-executive Chairperson since May 2025, separating the chair and CEO roles. The Board has three standing committees: Audit, Management Organization and Compensation, and Corporate Governance, with the Audit Committee leading risk oversight. Performance-based pay represented between 55% and 66% of named-executive-officer targeted compensation for fiscal 2025, long-term awards are predominantly performance-based, and annual cash incentives are capped at 200% of target. These features align pay with performance.
management.insiderOwnership: Insider ownership is modest relative to the outside institutional holders. As of March 9, 2026, all directors and executive officers as a group owned 2.89% of the class, or 1,276,149 shares, with director Gregg C. Sengstack holding 2.20%, or 971,803 shares, including exercisable options. CEO Joseph A. Ruzynski held 61,050 shares. The dominant institutional holders are BlackRock at 14.34% and The Vanguard Group at 9.80%, each reporting on Schedule 13F. Diane D. Humphrey is an individual holder with 6.05%, and the Company holds a right of first refusal over 2,362,118 of her shares. Executives are also subject to stock-ownership requirements.

idiosyncratic: Demand is cyclical and tied to housing starts and to the energy and mining industries; the 10-K names both as drivers of revenue, gross margin, and operating results. A downturn in either would pressure the premium 27.7x TTM multiple.
The company purchases most raw materials on the open market and does not generally hedge commodity or energy costs, so cost inflation that cannot be passed through would compress margins.

Tariffs on imports from Canada, Mexico, and China raise input costs and invite retaliation, and management calls the consolidated impact uncertain. The Q2'26 gross margin benefited from tariff refunds that may not recur.
Operations in Argentina and Turkey use highly inflationary accounting, and currency losses reduced results by $2.5M in Q2'26 and $2.1M for the six months.
A $4.5M legal settlement in Energy Systems cut that segment's Q2'26 operating margin to 34.8%, and further legal or restructuring charges could recur.
risks.systemic: Systemic risks are macro and policy-driven. Global trade policy and tariffs on imports from Canada, Mexico, and China raise input costs and could draw retaliatory tariffs, with an impact the company calls uncertain. Broader economic and interest-rate cycles drive the end markets, and a slowdown would cut demand across segments. Foreign-currency volatility, especially in highly inflationary Argentina and Turkey, affects reported results regardless of operating performance. The 10-K's January 2026 safe-harbor guidance under the OECD Pillar Two framework is expected to largely reduce its impact, and the company expects no material impact on its taxes now or in the future. These forces sit largely outside management's control.

body: The BUY rating rests on durable water and energy demand, a raised 2026 outlook, and a conservative, net-cash balance sheet, framed by a $105.00 to $125.00 target range against the $95.99 price. The quarter paired 6% top-line growth with an 18% rise in adjusted diluted EPS to $1.55, and management lifted full-year 2026 guidance. Steady free cash flow funds the dividend and continuing buybacks. The probability-weighted fair value sits above the current price and inside our target range.

The rating carries real risk. Valuation is full, the business is cyclical, and currency and tariff swings can move reported results regardless of operations. Our bear case, set out above, is a real scenario, not a formality. We would turn more cautious if the 2026 guidance slips or if the gross-margin benefit from tariff refunds reverses.
